office_does: A Clallam PUD commissioner is one of three board members who set policy and rates and hire the general manager for the public electric, water, wastewater and wholesale broadband utility serving Clallam County outside the City of Port Angeles; six-year term.
race_blurb: Open seat; appointee John Purvis is not running. Former commissioner Rick Paschall, who resigned in 2023 and led the District 2-only primary, faces first-time candidate Randy Brackett, a public-works engineer. Every PUD voter, which excludes the City of Port Angeles, can vote in November. Both put rates first; they differ on the base charge and on hydropower's future.

candidates.summary: Former District 2 commissioner (elected 2020, resigned 2023), with 31 years in power supply, trading and compliance, including at BPA and the Pacific Northwest Generating Cooperative. Led the primary with 43.5%.
highlights: Won the seat in 2020; resigned in early 2023, later citing a stroke he has recovered from [S6][S2]
Voted for the 2021 resolution opposing Snake River dam removal and for 2022-23 rate increases [S8][S7]
Top goal: keep rates as low as possible, citing BPA and compliance cost pressures [S1][S2]
Calls the fixed base charge high but fair; strongly supports hydropower [S2]

candidates.summary: Licensed professional engineer with 34 years in public works management in Northwest Washington and Alaska; first run for office. Second in the primary with 30.6%.
highlights: Says rates cannot keep rising 3.5% a year; criticizes the fixed base charge [S1][S5]
Warns a warming climate threatens hydropower; backs local generation and the Sequim microgrid [S1][S5]
Wants to keep pursuing grants and work collaboratively with BPA [S1]
Founding chair of Habitat for Humanity in Jefferson County [S1]
